# Smokescreen

> Smoke for Bevy 0.20 games that fills rooms, pours through doorways, stops at walls and blocks sight, with line-of-sight queries that agree with what players see. `bevy_smokescreen` is the Bevy plugin: it draws the smoke and adds components, messages and queries. `smokescreen` is the simulation underneath, with no engine in it and the same answers bit for bit on every machine, for dedicated servers, bots and other engines.

This file maps the API of `bevy_smokescreen` and `smokescreen` 0.2 for coding assistants, with recipes. Its Rust code is compiled against 0.2 as doc tests. Each published version of `bevy_smokescreen` carries its own copy at the root of its package.

- **Which crate.** A Bevy game depends on `bevy_smokescreen`, which re-exports the core as `bevy_smokescreen::smokescreen`. A headless server, bots or another engine depend on `smokescreen` alone (Rust 1.88 or newer; it depends only on `glam` and `libm`, and `serde` with its `serde` feature). In a workspace with both, `smokescreen = "0.2"` resolves to the version the plugin pins.
- **Versions.** `bevy_smokescreen` 0.2 is for Bevy 0.20 only, and needs Rust 1.97.1 or newer. Later 0.2 releases may add enum variants (`#[non_exhaustive]`: match with a `_` arm) and struct fields (build structs from a constructor or with `..default()`, as this file does); `CloudSpec` and `Impact` gain fields only in a new 0.x. Releases within 0.2 avoid changing results where they can, but run the same version on every machine in a match, serialised specs and impacts included.
- **Features.** `serde` (in both crates, off by default): `Serialize` and `Deserialize` on `CloudSpec`, `Impact`, `SmokeBullet` and `SmokeExplosion`, for networking crates. `webgpu` (the plugin): draw through WebGPU in a browser.
- **Imports.** `use bevy::prelude::*;` and `use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;` cover most code. `Config`, `ConfigError`, `Tuning`, `CloudSpec`, `CloudSource`, `CloudId`, `Impact`, `Smokes`, `Level`, `SmokeTimeline`, `HoleSettings` and `VoxelBytesError` are at the plugin's root (`bevy_smokescreen::Config`), not in the prelude. For the core alone: `use smokescreen::*;` and `use smokescreen::glam::Vec3;` (the same `Vec3` as Bevy's).
- **Units.** Positions, lengths and volumes are in your world's units: Y-up metres unless you choose others (recipe "Your own units"). The look's few lengths (`SmokeSettings::extinction`, per metre, and `noise_frequency`) are in metres whatever the units.
- **Rules and looks.** What hides what (the rules) must be the same on every machine in a match: the `Tuning` in the plugin's `Config`, the level, and each smoke's style (`DefaultSmokeStyle` or `Smoke::with_style`), volume, lifetime, grow time, start, fade time, seed, source and pop tick. The look may differ from machine to machine: `SmokeSettings`, a smoke's tint and density, each camera's quality dial.
- **Ticks.** The simulation runs on ticks (`Config::tick_rate`: 128 a second in the plugin by default), counted from Bevy's virtual time unless you drive `SmokeClock` yourself. Bullets, explosions and pops land on the current tick unless they bring their own (`SmokeBullet::tick`, `SmokeExplosion::tick`, `Smoke::with_pop_tick`, `Smoke::from_spec`; recipe "Multiplayer in Bevy").
- **GPU.** Volumetric and faceted smoke need compute shaders: native (Vulkan, Metal, DX12) or WebGPU. On WebGL2 the game keeps running with crystal smoke only.
- **Setup mistakes** are logged once each, with the fix ("Warnings the plugin logs" below).
- **Not API.** Items hidden from the docs on docs.rs may change in any release: `CloudState`, `CloudView`, `View::clouds`, `Smokes::internal_tuning`, `Smokes::pin_view` and `pinned_view`, what a `CloudShape` holds, and the core's `grid`, `light` and `math` modules. Don't use them.

## Setup

```toml
[dependencies]
bevy = "0.20"
bevy_smokescreen = "0.2"
```

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn main() {
    App::new()
        // After DefaultPlugins, whose renderer draws the smoke.
        .add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, SmokePlugin::default()))
        .add_systems(Startup, setup)
        .run();
}

fn setup(mut commands: Commands, mut meshes: ResMut<Assets<Mesh>>, mut materials: ResMut<Assets<StandardMaterial>>) {
    // Volumetric and faceted smoke are drawn only through cameras with SmokeCamera.
    commands.spawn((
        Camera3d::default(),
        bevy::camera::Hdr,
        SmokeCamera::HIGH, // the quality dial; HIGH is the default
        Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 1.7, -10.0).looking_at(Vec3::new(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), Vec3::Y),
    ));
    // The directional light that lights the smoke.
    commands.spawn((
        DirectionalLight::default(),
        SmokeSun,
        Transform::from_xyz(-4.0, 10.0, -6.0).looking_at(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::Y),
    ));
    // The level: smoke flows around every mesh marked SmokeObstacle. Include the floor.
    commands.spawn((
        Mesh3d(meshes.add(Plane3d::default().mesh().size(50.0, 50.0))),
        MeshMaterial3d(materials.add(Color::srgb(0.6, 0.6, 0.6))),
        SmokeObstacle,
    ));
    commands.spawn((
        Mesh3d(meshes.add(Cuboid::new(10.0, 3.0, 0.3))),
        MeshMaterial3d(materials.add(Color::srgb(0.5, 0.5, 0.55))),
        Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 1.5, 6.0),
        SmokeObstacle,
    ));
    // A smoke grenade popping at the origin.
    commands.spawn((Smoke::grenade(), Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)));
}
```

- `SmokePlugin::default()` simulates in Y-up metres at 128 ticks a second with the default rules. `SmokePlugin::new(config)` takes other units and rules (recipe "Your own units").
- `SmokeCamera` goes on every `Camera3d` that should see volumetric or faceted smoke. Crystal smoke is plain meshes, which any camera draws.
- `SmokeSun` marks the light that lights volumetric and faceted smoke. With only one directional light it can be left out.
- `SmokeObstacle` meshes are voxelised in the background whenever one is added, moved or removed, and new smokes wait for the first level. With no level at all, smoke knows only a flat ground at height 0 and passes through walls.
- A `Smoke` pops where its entity is, and the entity despawns itself when the cloud is gone.
- HDR cameras (`bevy::camera::Hdr`) are recommended; LDR cameras get an approximate tonemap.

## Recipes

### A smoke grenade where it lands

Spawn the `Smoke` when the grenade comes to rest. The cloud pops at the entity's position on the current tick and stays there: moving the entity later doesn't move it. The entity despawns when the cloud is gone (after 18 s by default); despawning it sooner removes the cloud at once.

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

/// Your game's message: a smoke grenade has come to rest.
#[derive(Message)]
struct GrenadeLanded {
    at: Vec3,
}

fn main() {
    App::new()
        .add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, SmokePlugin::default()))
        .add_message::<GrenadeLanded>()
        .add_systems(Update, pop_grenades)
        .run();
}

fn pop_grenades(mut landed: MessageReader<GrenadeLanded>, mut commands: Commands) {
    for grenade in landed.read() {
        // A 90 m³ cloud. Its seed comes from its position, so the same throw gives
        // the same cloud on every machine.
        commands.spawn((Smoke::grenade(), Transform::from_translation(grenade.at)));
    }
}
```

For a grenade with a fuse, spawn the `Smoke` when it lands and set `config.tuning.timeline.start` to the fuse time: the fill then runs while the grenade sits there.

### Sounds, effects and UI when a smoke pops and ends

The plugin triggers `SmokePopped` on a smoke's entity when its cloud pops, and `SmokeEnded` when the cloud is gone. Observe them for every smoke, as here, or for one with `.observe(…)` on its entity:

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

/// Your game's burst effect, and a minimap icon per smoke.
#[derive(Component)]
struct Burst;

#[derive(Component)]
struct MinimapIcon(Entity);

fn main() {
    App::new()
        .add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, SmokePlugin::default()))
        .add_observer(on_pop)
        .add_observer(on_end)
        .run();
}

fn on_pop(popped: On<SmokePopped>, clock: Res<SmokeClock>, world: Res<SmokeWorld>, mut commands: Commands) {
    commands.spawn(MinimapIcon(popped.entity));
    // A pop heard late (by a player who has just joined, say) comes with its own
    // tick: no burst once it is more than a quarter of a second old.
    if clock.tick.saturating_sub(popped.tick) > 32 {
        return;
    }
    if let Some(cloud) = world.cloud(popped.cloud) {
        // Placed and drawn this frame: the event comes before Bevy propagates transforms.
        commands.spawn((Burst, Transform::from_translation(cloud.spec().origin)));
    }
}

fn on_end(ended: On<SmokeEnded>, icons: Query<(Entity, &MinimapIcon)>, mut commands: Commands) {
    for (icon, smoke) in &icons {
        if smoke.0 == ended.entity {
            commands.entity(icon).despawn();
        }
    }
}
```

- Each comes once per smoke, with its entity, its `CloudId` and the tick. `SmokePopped` comes on the frame after the plugin popped the smoke, or once the clock reaches a pop tick still to come; the cloud starts to grow `Smoke::start` later (0.1 s by default). `SmokeEnded` comes when the clock reaches the cloud's end tick (it is no longer drawn and blocks nothing), after `SmokePopped` and before `despawn_when_done` despawns the entity, so the entity is still there to read.
- A smoke despawned sooner gets no `SmokeEnded`: observe Bevy's `On<Despawn>` for that.
- The cloud's origin is where the smoke popped, also for smokes made with `Smoke::from_spec`, whose entity may stand anywhere.

### Smoke walls, gas in a room, fog banks and steam

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn spawn_smokes(mut commands: Commands) {
    // A wall of smoke from the entity to 10 m along +X. Lasts 25 s.
    commands.spawn((Smoke::wall(Vec3::new(10.0, 0.0, 0.0)), Transform::from_xyz(-5.0, 0.3, 8.0)));
    // Poison gas filling a room 8 m × 3 m × 6 m: a box source centred on the entity,
    // with as much gas as the room holds. Walls marked SmokeObstacle keep it in.
    commands.spawn((
        Smoke::gas()
            .with_source(SmokeSource::Box {
                half_extents: Vec3::new(4.0, 1.5, 3.0),
            })
            .with_volume(8.0 * 3.0 * 6.0),
        Transform::from_xyz(14.0, 1.5, 18.0),
    ));
    // A fog bank fills a box for as long as its entity lives: despawn it to clear the fog.
    commands.spawn((Smoke::fog_bank(Vec3::new(6.0, 1.5, 4.0)), Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 1.5, 20.0)));
    // Steam from a vent, as crystals, tinted.
    commands.spawn((
        Smoke::steam_vent()
            .with_style(SmokeStyle::Crystal)
            .with_tint(Color::srgb(0.9, 0.95, 1.0)),
        Transform::from_xyz(8.0, 0.0, 0.0),
    ));
}
```

Every preset takes the builders `with_style`, `with_volume`, `with_lifetime`, `with_grow_time`, `with_start` (a fuse before it grows), `with_fade_time`, `with_seed`, `with_source` (`SmokeSource::Point`, `Line { offset }` or `Box { half_extents }`), `with_pop_tick`, `with_tint`, `with_density` and `with_despawn_when_done`. Tint and density are looks, and `with_despawn_when_done(false)` keeps the entity once the cloud is gone; the rest are rules. A line's offset and a box are in world axes: turning the entity doesn't turn them.

A source must fit the cloud's fill grid: with the default tuning 14.4 m × 7.2 m × 14.4 m (48 × 24 × 48 voxels of 0.3 m), 1.8 m of it below the source. So a box's half extents can be at most 7.2 m across and 1.8 m up, a line at most 14.4 m along each axis, and a volume at most about 1,490 m³. Bigger ones are cut off at the grid's faces (the log says so): use several smokes, or a larger `Tuning::grid_dims` or `Tuning::voxel_size`.

### Bullets and explosions

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

/// Forward your hitscan traces and explosions. Write the messages in Update (or anywhere
/// before SmokeSystems::Simulate, in PostUpdate): they land on the current tick.
fn forward_impacts(
    buttons: Res<ButtonInput<MouseButton>>,
    keys: Res<ButtonInput<KeyCode>>,
    mut bullets: MessageWriter<SmokeBullet>,
    mut explosions: MessageWriter<SmokeExplosion>,
) {
    if buttons.just_pressed(MouseButton::Left) {
        // From the muzzle to what the shot hit: a tunnel that closes within about 2 s.
        bullets.write(SmokeBullet {
            start: Vec3::new(0.0, 1.6, -10.0),
            end: Vec3::new(0.0, 1.0, 10.0),
            ..default()
        });
    }
    if keys.just_pressed(KeyCode::KeyH) {
        // An HE grenade: clears a sphere (3.5 m by default) that refills over about 5 s.
        explosions.write(SmokeExplosion {
            center: Vec3::new(0.0, 0.5, 3.0),
            ..default()
        });
    }
}
```

Holes count in the rule: a tunnel opens a line of sight until it closes. `Tuning::holes` sets their sizes and times (`None` turns them off), and `Tuning::max_holes_per_cloud` (16) how many count per smoke, the newest first. A message with a `tick` (`SmokeBullet { start, end, tick: Some(t) }`) lands on that tick instead of the current one: the shot's own, for a shot heard late or replayed. `radius: Some(r)` sets an explosion's size.

### Bot line of sight and muffled sound

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

#[derive(Component)]
struct Bot {
    /// Enemies the smoke doesn't hide from this bot.
    in_sight: usize,
}

#[derive(Component)]
struct Enemy;

fn bot_vision(
    vision: SmokeVision,
    mut bots: Query<(&GlobalTransform, &mut Bot)>,
    enemies: Query<&GlobalTransform, With<Enemy>>,
) {
    // Every smoke at this tick, asked from every thread at once.
    let view = vision.view();
    bots.par_iter_mut().for_each(|(bot, mut state)| {
        let eye = bot.translation() + Vec3::new(0.0, 1.6, 0.0);
        state.in_sight = enemies
            .iter()
            .filter(|enemy| {
                let head = enemy.translation() + Vec3::new(0.0, 1.7, 0.0);
                // True once the line passes through Tuning::sight_threshold of cloud
                // (0.8 m by default), every smoke added up.
                !view.blocks_sight(eye, head)
            })
            .count();
    });
}

/// How much of a sound gets through the smoke between its source and the listener.
fn muffle(vision: SmokeVision, listeners: Query<&GlobalTransform, With<Camera3d>>) {
    let source = Vec3::new(0.0, 1.0, 10.0);
    for ear in &listeners {
        let gain = vision.transmittance(source, ear.translation()); // 0..1
        let _ = gain; // feed it to your audio mixer
    }
}
```

`SmokeVision` answers for the current tick, in world units: `blocks_sight(a, b)`, `occlusion(a, b)` (the amount of cloud between two points), `transmittance(a, b)`, `density_at(p)` (every smoke added up) and `density_of(cloud, p)` (one smoke's). `view()` is that tick's `SmokeView`, `Copy + Sync`, with the same questions: take it once for many queries, `par_iter`, or your own functions. `drawn_view()` is the drawn tick's, for checks that must agree with the picture. A server without Bevy asks `smokescreen::Smokes` the same questions and gets the same answers.

`SmokeVision` only reads, so systems that use it run in parallel. It answers from views the plugin prepares when the clock moves (in `PreUpdate`) and again once the frame's pops and impacts are in (after `SmokeSystems::Simulate`): every system in `Update` sees the same smoke, whatever order they run in. A change made straight to `SmokeWorld` in `Update` shows from then on, or at once after `world.prepare_vision(&clock)`. For another tick (lag compensation), use `world.view(tick)` with `ResMut<SmokeWorld>`.

### Gas damage

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

/// Your marker on the gas smokes you spawn:
/// `commands.spawn((Smoke::gas(), Gas, Transform::from_translation(at)))`.
#[derive(Component)]
struct Gas;

#[derive(Component)]
struct Health(f32);

fn gas_damage(
    vision: SmokeVision,
    gas: Query<&Smoke, With<Gas>>,
    mut players: Query<(&GlobalTransform, &mut Health)>,
    time: Res<Time>,
) {
    for (player, mut health) in &mut players {
        let chest = player.translation() + Vec3::new(0.0, 1.2, 0.0);
        // Only the gas smokes' density: plain smoke at the same spot does no harm.
        let density: f32 = gas
            .iter()
            .filter_map(Smoke::cloud) // a smoke's CloudId, once it has popped
            .map(|cloud| vision.density_of(cloud, chest))
            .sum();
        health.0 -= 25.0 * density * time.delta_secs();
    }
}
```

`density_of(cloud, p)` is one smoke's density at a point, 0..1: volumetric smoke's density, and 1 inside a crystal or faceted puff. `density_at(p)` adds up every smoke's, gas or not. Asked per smoke, damage can also say whose gas it was. A server on the core alone asks `view.density_of(id, p)`, with the `CloudId` that `Smokes::pop` returned.

### The level from meshes, boxes or your own physics

Mark meshes with `SmokeObstacle` (Setup), or build the level yourself and insert it before smokes pop: a cloud keeps the shape it filled with.

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn load_level(mut commands: Commands) {
    // Boxes, for blockouts and tests.
    let walls = BoxObstacles::new(vec![ObstacleBox::from_center_size(
        Vec3::new(0.0, 1.5, 6.0),
        Vec3::new(10.0, 3.0, 0.3),
    )]);
    // Voxelised once, at the tuning's voxel size (0.3 m by default): every fill is then bit
    // lookups, and the clouds come out exactly as the boxes alone would make them.
    let level = VoxelObstacles::from_level(Vec3::new(-50.0, -2.0, -50.0), Vec3::new(50.0, 12.0, 50.0), 0.3, &walls);
    commands.insert_resource(SmokeLevel::new(level));
}

/// From your physics engine: is the box at `center`, `half` either side, blocked?
/// Also asked with a `half` of 0, as a point test.
fn level_from_physics(overlaps_box: impl Fn(Vec3, f32) -> bool) -> VoxelObstacles {
    VoxelObstacles::build(Vec3::new(-50.0, -2.0, -50.0), Vec3::new(50.0, 12.0, 50.0), 0.3, |center, half| {
        overlaps_box(center, half)
    })
}

/// Open ground on purpose: say so, and the log stops warning about a missing level.
fn open_ground(mut commands: Commands) {
    commands.insert_resource(SmokeLevel::new(FlatGround::new(0.0, UpAxis::Y)));
}
```

For multiplayer, voxelise once and ship the voxels (`VoxelObstacles::to_bytes`, `VoxelObstacles::from_bytes`), so every machine has the same level. `from_bytes` returns a `VoxelBytesError` for bytes it can't read (not voxels, a newer format, cut short, or nonsense), never a panic. `VoxelObstacles::from_triangles` voxelises meshes outside Bevy.

### A glTF level

`SmokeObstacle` marks only its own entity's mesh, and a glTF scene's meshes are its descendants. Mark each one once the scene has spawned:

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy::world_serialization::WorldInstanceReady;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn spawn_level(mut commands: Commands, assets: Res<AssetServer>) {
    commands
        .spawn(WorldAssetRoot(assets.load("level.glb#Scene0")))
        .observe(mark_level_meshes);
}

fn mark_level_meshes(
    ready: On<WorldInstanceReady>,
    children: Query<&Children>,
    meshes: Query<(), With<Mesh3d>>,
    mut commands: Commands,
) {
    for entity in children.iter_descendants(ready.entity) {
        if meshes.contains(entity) {
            commands.entity(entity).insert(SmokeObstacle);
        }
    }
}
```

`GltfAssetLabel::Scene(0).from_asset("level.glb")` is the same path. Smokes that pop before the scene has spawned find no level: start throwing smoke once the level exists (`run_if(resource_exists::<SmokeLevel>)`). The meshes must keep their data in the main world, as the glTF loader does by default.

With a Blender add-on (and its crate) that inserts registered components from glTF extras, you can mark the meshes in Blender instead: `SmokeObstacle` is reflected and registered. So are `Smoke` and the plugin's other components and resources, for inspectors and scene files too. A smoke's style is the one thing left out: it is the core's type, so a smoke from a scene takes `DefaultSmokeStyle`.

### The quality dial and budget mode

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn spawn_camera(mut commands: Commands) {
    // A fixed step: MINIMUM, LOWER, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH (the default) or ULTRA,
    // or any quality from 0 to 1 with SmokeCamera::with_quality(q).
    commands.spawn((Camera3d::default(), SmokeCamera::MEDIUM));
}

/// The dial can change at any time, from a settings menu say.
fn set_quality(keys: Res<ButtonInput<KeyCode>>, mut cameras: Query<&mut SmokeCamera>) {
    if keys.just_pressed(KeyCode::F1) {
        for mut camera in &mut cameras {
            camera.quality = 1.0; // ultra
        }
    }
}

/// What the dial chose (SmokeQuality comes with SmokeCamera), and what it cost.
fn show_quality(cameras: Query<&SmokeQuality>) {
    for quality in &cameras {
        info!("smoke at {}: {:?} ms of GPU time", quality.tier_name(), quality.measured_ms);
    }
}
```

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy::render::diagnostic::RenderDiagnosticsPlugin;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn main() {
    App::new()
        // Budget mode needs GPU timings: RenderDiagnosticsPlugin, on a backend with
        // timestamp queries (Vulkan or DX12).
        .add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, RenderDiagnosticsPlugin, SmokePlugin::default()))
        .add_systems(Startup, |mut commands: Commands| {
            // The best step that keeps this camera's smoke within 1.5 ms of GPU time.
            commands.spawn((Camera3d::default(), SmokeCamera::budget(1.5)));
        })
        .run();
}
```

No step of the dial changes a cloud's shape, only how precisely it is drawn, so a player at a cheaper step doesn't see through smoke that hides them at a better one. (One exception: the experimental faceted look's see-through bullet tunnels come out a few pixels wider at cheaper steps.) Crystal smoke has no dial.

### Picking a look

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn main() {
    App::new()
        .add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, SmokePlugin::default()))
        // The style of smokes that don't choose their own, read at each pop: a rule, the
        // same on every machine.
        .insert_resource(DefaultSmokeStyle(SmokeStyle::Volumetric))
        // The look, which can change at any time and differ from player to player: none of
        // it changes what hides what.
        .insert_resource(SmokeSettings {
            noise_within_rule: NoiseWithinRule::Capped,
            ..default()
        })
        .add_systems(Startup, |mut commands: Commands| {
            // One smoke in another look.
            commands.spawn((
                Smoke::grenade().with_style(SmokeStyle::Crystal),
                Transform::from_xyz(4.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            ));
        })
        .run();
}
```

- **Volumetric** (the default): soft and lit by the sun. On an Apple M4 at 1920×1080, one smoke adds 0.2 ms far away to 0.75 ms filling the screen, at the dial's best step. Its noise thins some smoke the rule counts, the same for every player. If a server, bots or abilities use the rule, set `noise_within_rule` to `Capped` (smoother inside, cheaper) or `Filled` (keeps the billows, costs more): then volumetric smoke at `Smoke::density` 1 or more never shows through what the rule blocks. (The gas, fog and steam presets draw thinner, at 0.5–0.6: a look only, so players see more through them than the rule allows.)
- **Crystal**: separate tumbling polyhedra drawn as ordinary meshes, about 0.1 ms. The cheapest to draw and to check. In a crystal-only game, `config.tuning.sight_threshold = 0.0` makes any contact block, and the picture and the rule then agree exactly.
- **Faceted**, experimental in 0.2: polyhedral puffs merged like metaballs. It costs 20–40 times what volumetric smoke costs to draw, and about 3 times more again with bullet tunnels.
- The style is a rule: every machine must give a smoke the same one, through `with_style` or the same `DefaultSmokeStyle`. A `match` on `SmokeStyle` needs a `_` arm: later versions may add styles.

### Your own units (Z-up inches)

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::Config;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn main() {
    // Everything the plugin takes or gives is now in Z-up inches: transforms, messages,
    // SmokeVision. Config::new converts the default rules (Tuning::new).
    let mut config = Config::new(Units::INCHES_Z_UP, 64.0);
    config.tuning.sight_threshold = 32.0; // 32 inches of cloud hide a player
    App::new()
        .add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, SmokePlugin::new(config)))
        .add_systems(Startup, |mut commands: Commands| {
            commands.spawn((
                Camera3d::default(),
                SmokeCamera::HIGH,
                Transform::from_xyz(0.0, -400.0, 64.0).looking_at(Vec3::new(0.0, 0.0, 40.0), Vec3::Z),
            ));
            commands.spawn((Smoke::grenade(), Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)));
        })
        .run();
}
```

Any other units: `Units::new(UpAxis::Z, metres_per_unit)`. The core works in metres internally and gives the same smoke in every unit system. The look's `extinction` (per metre) and `noise_frequency` (tiles per metre) stay in metres; `wind` is in your units.

### Multiplayer in Bevy

When a server decides the smoke, drive the smoke's clock from your netcode, and spawn each cloud the server announces from its `CloudSpec`:

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::CloudSpec;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

/// Stand-in for your netcode's state.
#[derive(Resource, Default)]
struct Net {
    server_tick: u64,
    interpolation_tick: u64,
    interpolation_fraction: f32,
    /// Pops the server announced: each spec carries its pop tick. The colour is your
    /// look (a team's colour, say).
    pops: Vec<(CloudSpec, Color)>,
    /// Shots the server announced: start, end and tick.
    bullets: Vec<(Vec3, Vec3, u64)>,
}

fn main() {
    App::new()
        .add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, SmokePlugin::default()))
        .init_resource::<Net>()
        // The clock follows your netcode instead of Bevy's virtual time.
        .insert_resource(SmokeClock { auto: false, ..default() })
        .add_systems(Update, sync_smoke)
        .run();
}

fn sync_smoke(
    mut net: ResMut<Net>,
    mut clock: ResMut<SmokeClock>,
    mut world: ResMut<SmokeWorld>,
    mut bullets: MessageWriter<SmokeBullet>,
    mut commands: Commands,
) {
    clock.tick = net.server_tick; // fills advance to it, and SmokeVision answers for it
    clock.draw_tick = Some(net.interpolation_tick); // the tick drawn
    clock.draw_fraction = net.interpolation_fraction; // how far the frame is past it
    // The plugin prepared SmokeVision's views of the old ticks in PreUpdate: these
    // ones from here on. (A clock written in First needs none of this.)
    world.prepare_vision(&clock);
    // Events with their own ticks may arrive late or out of order: every machine
    // computes the same clouds from the same events.
    for (spec, tint) in net.pops.drain(..) {
        // The server's cloud to the bit, however late it is heard, with your look. The
        // entity despawns once the cloud is gone; despawn it sooner to remove the cloud.
        commands.spawn(Smoke::from_spec(spec).with_tint(tint));
    }
    for (start, end, tick) in net.bullets.drain(..) {
        // The tunnel the shot opened on its own tick, however late it is heard.
        bullets.write(SmokeBullet {
            start,
            end,
            tick: Some(tick),
        });
    }
}
```

- Send each pop's `CloudSpec` (origin, pop tick, seed, style, source, volume, timeline: a couple of dozen bytes) and each bullet and explosion with its tick. A server running the plugin finds the spec of a smoke it popped with `world.cloud(id).map(|c| *c.spec())`, the id from `Smoke::cloud()`.
- With `bevy_smokescreen`'s `serde` feature, `CloudSpec`, `Impact`, `SmokeBullet` and `SmokeExplosion` implement `Serialize` and `Deserialize`, as networking crates' events need (bevy_replicon, lightyear). Binary formats such as postcard and bincode carry every number exactly, and so does `serde_json` for every finite `f32`. Both ends must run the same version.
- Every machine needs the same `Tuning` (in `SmokePlugin::new(config)`), the same `DefaultSmokeStyle` (or a style on every smoke) and the same level: voxelise once and ship `VoxelObstacles::to_bytes`.
- `Smoke::from_spec(spec)` takes everything that decides the cloud from the spec, not from the entity's position or the clock: give it a `Transform` at `spec.origin` if anything else needs its position (a sound, say). Tint and `density` are yours, and `Smoke::cloud()` gives its id for `SmokeVision::density_of`.
- When every machine spawns the same `Smoke` from the same event instead (lockstep, rollback), give it the event's tick: `Smoke::gas().with_pop_tick(tick)`. Spawn it unparented at the same position: a parent's transform is applied in floating point, so the position, and the seed made from it, may come out in other bits.
- `SmokeWorld` is the core's `Smokes` the plugin runs (it derefs to it). Clouds popped or inserted on it directly are drawn with the default look (no tint) until they end or `world.remove(id)`. `world.bullet(start, end, tick)` and `world.explosion(center, radius, tick)` do what the ticked messages do, from a system that holds `ResMut<SmokeWorld>`.
- A view of a recent past tick answers as it would have then (lag compensation): `world.view(tick).blocks_sight(a, b)`. Clouds and holes are kept for `Config::history_ticks` (a second by default) after they end, `Smoke` entities' clouds included.
- A clock moved after `PreUpdate` (as here, or once per fixed step in `FixedUpdate`) needs `world.prepare_vision(&clock)` after it, or `SmokeVision` answers for the tick before and the log says so once.

### A player who joins mid-match

A late joiner needs the clouds still alive and every bullet and explosion the server's world still keeps. `world.impacts()` gives those back exactly as they were given, in your units: the world works in metres inside, and converting back wouldn't always give the same bits.

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::{CloudSpec, Impact};

/// What the server sends a player who joins at `tick`.
struct CatchUp {
    specs: Vec<CloudSpec>,
    impacts: Vec<Impact>,
}

/// On the server.
fn catch_up(world: &SmokeWorld, tick: u64) -> CatchUp {
    CatchUp {
        // Clouds that ended are kept a little longer (`Config::history_ticks`): leave them out.
        specs: world.clouds().filter(|c| c.end_tick() > tick).map(|c| *c.spec()).collect(),
        impacts: world.impacts().collect(),
    }
}

/// On the player's machine, once its clock runs on the server's ticks.
fn join(catch_up: CatchUp, world: &mut SmokeWorld, commands: &mut Commands) {
    for spec in catch_up.specs {
        commands.spawn(Smoke::from_spec(spec));
    }
    for impact in catch_up.impacts {
        // Any kind of impact, whatever later versions add.
        world.impact(impact);
    }
}
```

Its clouds then match the server's to the bit, holes included, and `SmokePopped` comes with each cloud's own pop tick, so the player's sounds can leave out pops long past. With the `serde` feature, `CatchUp` can derive `Serialize` and `Deserialize`.

### A dedicated server in Bevy

A server runs the plugin without a window, a renderer or assets: it simulates and answers `SmokeVision`, and does none of the drawing's work.

```rust,no_run
use std::time::Duration;

use bevy::{app::ScheduleRunnerPlugin, prelude::*};
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn main() {
    // The level every machine shares, voxelised once (`VoxelObstacles::to_bytes`).
    let bytes = std::fs::read("level.voxels").expect("the level");
    let level = VoxelObstacles::from_bytes(&bytes).expect("the level's voxels");
    App::new()
        .add_plugins((
            // A frame per tick, and nothing to draw with.
            MinimalPlugins.set(ScheduleRunnerPlugin::run_loop(Duration::from_secs_f64(1.0 / 128.0))),
            // Places smokes where their entities are.
            TransformPlugin,
            SmokePlugin::default(),
        ))
        .insert_resource(SmokeLevel::new(level))
        .run();
}
```

- `TransformPlugin` is part of `DefaultPlugins`, not `MinimalPlugins`. Without it nothing updates `GlobalTransform`, so smokes placed by their entity would pop at the origin (the log says so). Smokes made with `Smoke::from_spec` need no transforms.
- `SmokeObstacle` works on a server too, given Bevy's `AssetPlugin` and `MeshPlugin` and the level's meshes. Shipping the voxels is lighter and gives every machine the same level.
- Drive the clock from your netcode as in "Multiplayer in Bevy", and answer gameplay questions with `SmokeVision` as in a game.

### A first-person weapon inside smoke

Smoke is drawn over everything the world camera drew, a weapon half a metre from the eye included. Draw the weapon with a second camera after it, without `SmokeCamera`:

```rust,no_run
use bevy::camera::ClearColorConfig;
use bevy::camera::visibility::RenderLayers;
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

const WEAPON_LAYER: usize = 1;

fn spawn_player(mut commands: Commands, mut meshes: ResMut<Assets<Mesh>>, mut materials: ResMut<Assets<StandardMaterial>>) {
    commands
        .spawn((Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 1.6, -3.5), Visibility::default()))
        .with_children(|player| {
            // The world camera: the level and the smoke.
            player.spawn((Camera3d::default(), SmokeCamera::HIGH));
            // The weapon camera: drawn after the world camera, over its picture, and only
            // the weapon's layer.
            player.spawn((
                Camera3d::default(),
                Camera {
                    order: 1,
                    clear_color: ClearColorConfig::None,
                    ..default()
                },
                RenderLayers::layer(WEAPON_LAYER),
            ));
            player.spawn((
                Mesh3d(meshes.add(Cuboid::new(0.08, 0.1, 0.6))),
                MeshMaterial3d(materials.add(Color::srgb(0.15, 0.15, 0.17))),
                Transform::from_xyz(0.22, -0.2, -0.45),
                RenderLayers::layer(WEAPON_LAYER),
            ));
        });
    // Light the world and the weapon.
    commands.spawn((
        DirectionalLight::default(),
        SmokeSun,
        RenderLayers::from_layers(&[0, WEAPON_LAYER]),
        Transform::from_xyz(-4.0, 10.0, -6.0).looking_at(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::Y),
    ));
}
```

### A dedicated server on the core alone

```toml
[dependencies]
smokescreen = "0.2"
```

```rust
use smokescreen::glam::Vec3;
use smokescreen::*;

/// Your game's collision behind the Level trait, in your units: here boxes in Z-up
/// inches, as (min, max), on a floor at z = 0.
struct Brushes(Vec<(Vec3, Vec3)>);

impl Level for Brushes {
    /// Is the cube at `center`, `half` either side, blocked?
    fn is_blocked(&self, center: Vec3, half: f32) -> bool {
        center.z < half
            || self
                .0
                .iter()
                .any(|(lo, hi)| (center + half).cmpgt(*lo).all() && (center - half).cmplt(*hi).all())
    }

    /// Only renderers ask this, for lighting; a server never does.
    fn ray_hit(&self, _origin: Vec3, _dir: Vec3, _max_dist: f32) -> bool {
        false
    }
}

fn main() {
    // Your units and tick rate; the rules in those units.
    let mut config = Config::new(Units::INCHES_Z_UP, 64.0);
    config.tuning.sight_threshold = 32.0; // 32 inches of cloud hide a player
    let walls = Brushes(vec![(Vec3::new(-400.0, 300.0, 0.0), Vec3::new(400.0, 320.0, 160.0))]);
    let mut smokes = Smokes::new(config, walls);

    // Events from your game simulation, each with its tick.
    let origin = Vec3::new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
    smokes.pop(CloudSpec::new(origin, 0, CloudSpec::seed_from_origin(origin), Style::Volumetric));
    for tick in 0..=2 * 64 {
        smokes.advance(tick); // every tick: the fills spend their budget
    }
    // Two seconds later the cloud has grown: it hides one player from the other.
    let (eye, enemy) = (Vec3::new(-400.0, 0.0, 64.0), Vec3::new(400.0, 0.0, 64.0));
    let view = smokes.view(2 * 64); // Copy + Sync: share it between threads
    assert!(view.blocks_sight(eye, enemy));
    // A shot along the line opens a tunnel through the smoke for a while.
    smokes.bullet(eye, enemy, 2 * 64);
}
```

- A cloud at tick *t* is a pure function of its `CloudSpec`, the level, the `Tuning` and *t*, and holes are events with ticks: send them to clients, and every machine computes the same clouds. Events may arrive late or out of order, and late joiners catch up from the same events: the specs of the clouds still alive, and `smokes.impacts()`, every bullet and explosion the world keeps, exactly as given (`smokes.impact(i)` adds each back).
- `Level::is_inside(point)` defaults to `is_blocked(point, 0.0)`; override it if a box of size zero isn't a point test in your collision code.
- `fill_cloud(&config, &spec, &level)` runs a whole fill outside the world (on a worker thread, say) and gives a `CloudShape` for `Smokes::insert`. A `CloudShape` has no wire format: between machines, send the `CloudSpec`.
- `Config::fill_budget` is the fill work per tick (about 0.2 ms on a small cloud VM, under 0.1 ms on an Apple M4). It grows only when a fill wouldn't otherwise be ready by the time its cloud starts, and the finished cloud is the same however the work is split.

## Gotchas

- **Compute shaders.** Volumetric and faceted smoke need them: native, or WebGPU in a browser (Bevy's `webgpu` feature, or `bevy_smokescreen`'s). On WebGL2 only crystal smoke is drawn, and the log says why.
- **Transparent objects behind smoke show through it.** Alpha-blended objects (tracers, muzzle-flash sprites, particles) behind or inside volumetric or faceted smoke draw over it at full strength: Bevy draws them after the smoke, which writes no depth. Opaque and `AlphaMode::Mask` objects are hidden properly, crystal smoke hides everything, and transparent objects in front of a smoke are fine. For effects that must stay hidden, use one of those, or hide them where `blocks_sight(camera, effect)`.
- **`SmokeVision` sees the smoke as the plugin last prepared it**: when the clock moved in `PreUpdate`, and again after `SmokeSystems::Simulate`. Changes made straight to `SmokeWorld` show from then on, and a clock moved later needs `world.prepare_vision(&clock)`.
- **A first-person weapon needs its own camera** (recipe above), or smoke draws over it.
- **Orthographic cameras** draw no volumetric or faceted smoke; crystal smoke works.
- **Bevy 0.20 only.** `bevy_smokescreen` 0.1 and 0.2 are both for Bevy 0.20.
- **At most `Tuning::max_clouds` smokes count at once** (32): past that the oldest stop counting and aren't drawn, a long-lived fog bank first. At most 32 volumetric or faceted smokes are drawn at once; raise `max_clouds` past 32 only for crystal smoke.
- **The level comes first.** A cloud keeps the shape it filled with: closing a door doesn't re-shape a smoke, and clouds don't drift with wind.
- **Floors.** A single sheet facing up (a `Plane3d`) counts as ground, solid all the way down: use a box for a raised floor with air below it. Meshes need triangles facing outwards, as Bevy's shapes have; against inward-facing meshes and single upright sheets, smoke stops up to half a voxel short.
- **Mesh data must stay in the main world** for `SmokeObstacle` (the default; not `RenderAssetUsages::RENDER_WORLD` alone).
- **Lights.** Volumetric and faceted smoke take one directional light (`SmokeSun`) and up to 8 point lights, unshadowed; spot lights don't light them. Crystal smoke takes any light. A camera lit by an environment map or its own `AmbientLight` needs `SmokeSettings::ambient_override` set to match.
- **Faceted is experimental in 0.2**: costly to draw (see "Picking a look").
- **Safari 26** can't compile Bevy 0.20's `StandardMaterial` shader for meshes with UVs (Bevy's shader, not the smoke's): textured meshes need a fix in Bevy.

## Warnings the plugin logs

Each is logged once per app, with what to do. If a log shows one:

- "No active camera has SmokeCamera": add `SmokeCamera` to the `Camera3d` that should see smoke.
- "SmokeCamera is on an orthographic camera": use a perspective projection there, or crystal smoke.
- "The camera … has its own AmbientLight" or "… is lit by an environment map": set `SmokeSettings::ambient_override`.
- "SmokeCamera::budget_ms needs GPU timings": add `RenderDiagnosticsPlugin`, on Vulkan or DX12.
- "… directional lights have SmokeSun" or "… directional lights and none has SmokeSun": keep `SmokeSun` on exactly one.
- "A smoke popped with no level": mark the level's meshes, floor included, with `SmokeObstacle`, or insert a `SmokeLevel` before smokes pop; for open ground on purpose, `SmokeLevel::new(FlatGround::new(height, UpAxis::Y))`.
- "A smoke's box source …", "A smoke's line source …" or "A smoke asks for a volume of …, more than its fill grid holds": a smaller source or several smokes, or a larger `grid_dims` or `voxel_size`.
- "A smoke popped inside solid level geometry": pop smokes in open air, on or just above the floor. If every smoke does this, check that the level's meshes face outwards.
- "More smokes are alive than Tuning::max_clouds": fewer at once, or a larger `max_clouds` (past 32, crystal smoke only).
- "More than 32 volumetric or faceted smokes count at once" or "Tuning::max_clouds is …, but at most 32 …": keep `max_clouds` at 32 or less, or use crystal smoke for the rest.
- "More than 512 holes are open in the smokes drawn": keep `max_holes_per_cloud` × the smokes drawn at once within 512.
- "SmokeObstacle is on an entity without a Mesh3d": put it on the mesh entities themselves (recipe "A glTF level").
- "A SmokeObstacle mesh … has no triangle data in the main world": use a triangle list, loaded with `RenderAssetUsages::MAIN_WORLD`.
- "A SmokeObstacle mesh failed to load": fix the asset, or take `SmokeObstacle` off that entity; smokes wait for the level until then.
- "SmokePlugin was added before Bevy's RenderPlugin": add it after `DefaultPlugins`.
- "Bevy's TransformPlugin isn't added": add `TransformPlugin` (part of `DefaultPlugins`; a server on `MinimalPlugins` needs it), or make every smoke with `Smoke::from_spec`.
- "SmokeVision answered for tick …, but SmokeClock is at …": write `SmokeClock` in `First`, or call `world.prepare_vision(&clock)` after writing it.
- A panic "SmokePlugin: Config::… is …": fix that setting. `Config::validate()` checks a configuration without panicking (one read from a file, say).
- "The GPU device … offers no compute shaders": WebGL2; in a browser, build with WebGPU. Crystal smoke still works.

## API: bevy_smokescreen

In `bevy_smokescreen::prelude` unless marked "root".

- [SmokePlugin](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokePlugin.html): the plugin. `SmokePlugin::default()` or `SmokePlugin::new(config)`; add it after `DefaultPlugins`.
- [Smoke](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.Smoke.html): component, a cloud popping where its entity is. Presets `grenade()`, `wall(offset)`, `gas()`, `fog_bank(half_extents)`, `steam_vent()`; `from_spec(spec)`, exactly the cloud a server announced; builders `with_style`, `with_volume`, `with_lifetime`, `with_grow_time`, `with_start`, `with_fade_time`, `with_seed`, `with_source`, `with_pop_tick`, `with_tint`, `with_density`, `with_despawn_when_done`; `cloud()` gives its `CloudId` once popped (for `SmokeVision::density_of`). Reflected, all but `style`.
- [SmokeSource](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/enum.SmokeSource.html): `Point`, `Line { offset }`, `Box { half_extents }`, in world axes.
- [SmokeStyle](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/enum.SmokeStyle.html): `Volumetric` (the default), `Crystal`, `Faceted` (experimental). The core's `Style`.
- [DefaultSmokeStyle](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.DefaultSmokeStyle.html): resource, the style of smokes that don't choose their own, read at each pop: a rule, the same on every machine. `DefaultSmokeStyle(SmokeStyle::Crystal)`.
- [SmokeCamera](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeCamera.html): component for each `Camera3d` that should see smoke, with its quality dial. `MINIMUM`, `LOWER`, `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH` (the default), `ULTRA`, `with_quality(q)`, `budget(ms)`; fields `quality`, `budget_ms`, `temporal_jitter` (on with TAA), `measured_depth`, and `volumetric` and `facets` to pin the dial's knobs.
- [SmokeQuality](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/quality/struct.SmokeQuality.html): component that comes with `SmokeCamera`: what the dial chose. `tier`, `tier_name()`, `measured_ms`, `predicted_ms`.
- [SmokeSun](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeSun.html): marks the directional light that lights the smoke.
- [SmokeObstacle](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeObstacle.html): marks level meshes the smoke flows around.
- [SmokeLevel](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeLevel.html): resource, the level as any `Level`: `SmokeLevel::new(level)`. `SmokeObstacle` builds it, or insert your own.
- [SmokeBullet](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeBullet.html) and [SmokeExplosion](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeExplosion.html): messages, a tunnel along a shot (`start`, `end`) and a cleared sphere (`center`, `radius`), each on the current tick or its own `tick`. Build them with `..default()`.
- [SmokePopped](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokePopped.html) and [SmokeEnded](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeEnded.html): entity events for observers, once per smoke, when its cloud pops and when it is gone (before the entity despawns): `entity`, `cloud`, `tick`.
- [SmokeVision](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeVision.html): system parameter for gameplay queries at the current tick, read-only: `blocks_sight(a, b)`, `occlusion(a, b)`, `transmittance(a, b)`, `density_at(p)`, `density_of(cloud, p)`, `tick()`, and `view()` and `drawn_view()` for the tick's and the drawn tick's `SmokeView`.
- [SmokeView](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeView.html): every smoke at one tick, `Copy + Sync`, the core's `View`: the same questions from any number of threads.
- [SmokeSettings](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeSettings.html): resource, the look, which can change at any time and differ from player to player: `extinction`, `albedo`, `noise_within_rule`, `ambient_override`, `wind`, `crystal_shadows`, the noise, and debug views.
- [NoiseWithinRule](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/enum.NoiseWithinRule.html): `Off` (the default), `Capped`, `Filled`.
- [SmokeClock](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeClock.html): resource, the tick: `tick`, `draw_tick`, `draw_fraction`, `auto`.
- [SmokeWorld](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeWorld.html): resource, the core's `Smokes` the plugin runs (it derefs to it): pops, holes and queries at any tick. `prepare_vision(&clock)` prepares `SmokeVision`'s views again after the clock or the world changed mid-frame.
- [SmokeSystems](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/enum.SmokeSystems.html): system sets in `PostUpdate`, after transform propagation: `Simulate` (it ends by preparing `SmokeVision`'s views again), then `PrepareRender` (only with Bevy's renderer).
- [CrystalPuff](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.CrystalPuff.html): marks the entities the plugin spawns for crystal puffs.
- [quality](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/quality/index.html): the dial's steps: `VolumetricQuality` and `FacetQuality` (the knobs at each step, to pin with `SmokeCamera::volumetric` and `facets`), `TIER_NAMES`. `SmokeResolution` is the fraction of the screen's resolution volumetric smoke is marched at.
- Root: `Config`, `ConfigError`, `Tuning`, `CloudSpec`, `CloudSource`, `CloudId`, `Impact`, `Smokes`, `Level`, `SmokeTimeline` (the core's `Timeline`), `HoleSettings`, `SharedLevel`, `VoxelBytesError`, and the core itself as `bevy_smokescreen::smokescreen`.

## API: smokescreen

- [Smokes](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.Smokes.html): the world of clouds. `new(config, level)` (it panics on a config `Config::validate` refuses), `pop(spec)`, `bullet(start, end, tick)`, `explosion(center, radius, tick)`, `impact(i)`, `impacts()` (for late joiners), `advance(tick)`, `view(tick)`, and `blocks_sight`, `occlusion`, `density_at`, `density_of` at a tick; `insert(spec, shape)`, `remove(id)`, `clear()`, `set_level(level)`, `clouds()`, `cloud(id)`, `pending_fills()`.
- [View](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.View.html): every cloud at one tick, `Copy + Sync`: `blocks_sight`, `occlusion`, `density_at`, `density_of`, `tick`. Allocates nothing.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.Config.html): `Config::new(units, tick_rate)`; `tuning`, `fill_budget`, `level_query_units`, `history_ticks`, `cached_ticks`. `validate()` gives a [ConfigError](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.ConfigError.html) (`field()`, and a message) for a number that isn't finite; a tick rate, unit length, voxel size or volume not above 0; a `floor_fraction` outside 0 to 1; or a grid of more than `MAX_GRID_VOXELS`.
- [Tuning](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.Tuning.html): the rules, the same on every machine. `Tuning::new(&units)`; `grid_dims`, `voxel_size`, `volume`, `up_cost`, `down_cost`, `lumpiness`, `lump_size`, `floor_fraction`, `timeline`, `facets`, `crystals`, `facet_rule`, `volume_steps`, `holes`, `max_holes_per_cloud`, `max_clouds`, `sight_threshold`.
- [CloudSpec](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.CloudSpec.html): a pop, all a server has to send. `new(origin, pop_tick, seed, style)`, `with_source(source)`, `with_volume(volume)`, `with_timeline(timeline)`, `seed_from_origin(origin)`; fields `source`, `volume`, `timeline`. In Bevy, spawn one with `Smoke::from_spec`.
- [CloudSource](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.CloudSource.html): `Point`, `Line { end }`, `Box { half_extents }`.
- [Impact](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.Impact.html): a bullet or an explosion with its tick, as given: `Bullet { start, end, tick }`, `Explosion { center, radius, tick }`, `tick()`. What `Smokes::impacts()` gives back and `Smokes::impact(i)` takes.
- [Style](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.Style.html): `Volumetric`, `Faceted` (experimental), `Crystal`.
- [Level](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/trait.Level.html): trait for level geometry: `is_blocked(center, half_extent)`, `ray_hit(origin, dir, max_dist)`, and `is_inside(point)`, which has a default.
- [FlatGround](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.FlatGround.html), [BoxObstacles](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.BoxObstacles.html) with [ObstacleBox](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.ObstacleBox.html), and [VoxelObstacles](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.VoxelObstacles.html): ready-made levels. `VoxelObstacles::build`, `from_level`, `from_triangles`, `to_bytes`, `from_bytes` (a [VoxelBytesError](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.VoxelBytesError.html) for bytes it can't read).
- [Units](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.Units.html) and [UpAxis](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.UpAxis.html): `Units::METRES_Y_UP`, `Units::INCHES_Z_UP`, `Units::new(up, metres_per_unit)`.
- [Timeline](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.Timeline.html): a cloud's life in seconds: `start`, `grow_time`, `lifetime`, `fade_time`.
- [HoleSettings](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.HoleSettings.html): bullet tunnels' and explosions' sizes and times.
- [FacetSettings](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.FacetSettings.html), [FacetRule](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.FacetRule.html) (`Exact`, `Chords`, `Core`), [FacetLimits](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.FacetLimits.html), [ShapeMix](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.ShapeMix.html), [Polyhedron](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.Polyhedron.html) and [VolumeSteps](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.VolumeSteps.html) (`Voxel`, `HalfVoxel`): puff shapes, and how the rule counts faceted and volumetric clouds.
- [fill_cloud](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/fn.fill_cloud.html) and [CloudShape](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.CloudShape.html): a fill on the server, sent to clients for `Smokes::insert`.
- [CloudId](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.CloudId.html) and [CloudInfo](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.CloudInfo.html): a cloud's handle (not shared between machines), and what `clouds()` and `cloud(id)` give: `id`, `spec`, `timeline`, `start_tick`, `end_tick`, `age`.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/VagabondTech/smokescreen/blob/main/README.md): the guide: looks, presets, gameplay, multiplayer and servers, performance, every setting, limitations.
- [bevy_smokescreen on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2) and [smokescreen on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2): the API.
- [examples/minimal.rs](https://github.com/VagabondTech/smokescreen/blob/main/examples/minimal.rs): the smallest integration, with bullets, explosions and a bot's line of sight.
- [examples/presets.rs](https://github.com/VagabondTech/smokescreen/blob/main/examples/presets.rs): every preset and look, in a yard of `SmokeObstacle` meshes.
- [examples/viewmodel.rs](https://github.com/VagabondTech/smokescreen/blob/main/examples/viewmodel.rs): a first-person weapon that stays visible inside smoke.
- [examples/units.rs](https://github.com/VagabondTech/smokescreen/blob/main/examples/units.rs): the same scene in Y-up metres and Z-up inches.
- [smokescreen/examples/server.rs](https://github.com/VagabondTech/smokescreen/blob/main/smokescreen/examples/server.rs): a headless server loop with 250 bots.
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/VagabondTech/smokescreen/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each version.
